$about: The form family migrated from React Aria to Base UI 1.7.0: text-field, text-area, search-field, radio-group, form, input-group, link, separator, description-list. Every claim here is from a render (renderToStaticMarkup or @testing-library render) or from reading the installed dist, never from a docs page. Branch experiment/base-ui.
proof: packages/ui/src/form-family.test.tsx — 24 assertions, of which 7 grade SERVED HTML with the shipped gate rules (namedControls, resolvedIdrefs) and 2 assert a capability GAP so that an upstream fix turns the suite red rather than leaving a workaround in place forever. Plus packages/ui/src/input-group.test.tsx, unedited, and packages/ui/src/ssr-field-wiring.test.tsx and coverage.test.ts, unedited.

the_structural_change.what: form.tsx now owns the server-safe field wiring for the whole library rather than each component calling useFieldWiring itself.
the_structural_change.before: checkbox.tsx, switch.tsx and number-field.tsx each call useFieldWiring and spread four prop objects by hand, and each had to rediscover the same three rules: an explicit aria-label suppresses the naming arm, an id may only be minted for content that actually renders, and description+error share one aria-describedby in that order.
the_structural_change.after: <Field> calls the hook once and publishes the result on a Lumo context. <Label>, <Description> and <FieldError> read it and take no wiring props at all; the control reads it via useFieldControl(), or simply uses <FieldInput>. A component built on <Field> is server-named by construction rather than by remembering.

react_aria_fallback.why: date-picker.tsx, date-range-picker.tsx, time-field.tsx and date-field.tsx are still React Aria roots that render these three as children and depend on RAC's LabelContext / TextContext / FieldErrorContext. Making the three unconditionally Base UI would silently unname all four, in the same self-healing jsdom-invisible way this whole file exists to prevent.
react_aria_fallback.expiry: Deleted when the date family migrates. Nothing else in the tree reaches it — every other caller is inside a <Field>.
react_aria_fallback.precedent: FOCUS_RING / FOCUS_RING_SELF, which the same file already keeps in both spellings for the same reason.

the_structural_change.side_effect_fixed: number-field.tsx's own header records that its <FieldError> renders NOTHING because RAC's FieldError needs a FieldErrorContext nothing provides under Base UI. That defect is closed by this change without touching number-field.tsx: FieldError inside a <Field> is Base UI's Field.Error with `match`.

form.tsx.vendor_available: base-vega ships an item named `form` with an EMPTY files array — {name, type, $schema} and nothing else. There is nothing to vendor.

api_changes.was: RAC's per-Form prop, overridden to 'aria' so the browser's own English constraint message never appears on a Persian page.
api_changes.now: Mapped onto noValidate. Base UI's Form emits noValidate unconditionally in its default props (form/Form.mjs:91), so 'aria' is now the engine's own behaviour and 'native' is reachable because caller props merge AFTER the defaults.
api_changes.reason: Base UI has no aria/native vocabulary; its Form has validationMode: onSubmit|onBlur|onChange, which is a different axis (WHEN, not WHOSE MESSAGE).
RAC-specific props (validationErrors, onReset semantics) have no Base UI counterpart. Every prop the blocks actually pass — onSubmit, className — is a native form attribute and survives.

text-field.tsx.vendor_available: No base-vega text-field/input item was fetched for this pass; the composition is Lumo's COMPOSED shape (required label) and upstream's is compositional, which is the same disqualifier input-group.tsx already records.

state_selectors.data-hovered: → hover:. Zero files in the whole 1.7.0 dist declare data-hovered. Cost: jsdom models no pointer, so this rule loses its unit tier.
state_selectors.data-invalid: UNCHANGED. InputDataAttributes declares `invalid` with the caveat 'when wrapped in Field.Root', and this component always renders one. Verified by render: aria-invalid=true and data-invalid on the input at SSR.
state_selectors.focus-visible: Untouched — an <input> is its own focusable element, so theme.css's single :where([data-lumo]):focus-visible rule still draws it. FOCUS_RING_SELF is not needed here.

api_changes.reason: Base UI decides validation timing on <Form> and Field.Root, not per control, and its vocabulary is onSubmit/onBlur/onChange.
No equivalent. tabIndex={-1} reaches the input directly and is what this ever meant.

api_changes.kind: signature PRESERVED, and this was not free elsewhere
api_changes.reason: RAC's onChange hands over a string. Base UI's Field.Control has onValueChange(value: string, details), so the string survives — unlike the usual event/value mismatch a swap like this produces.

text-area.tsx.note: Base UI has NO textarea part — `input` is the only member of that family among 83 export subpaths. The replacement is the render prop, which keeps data-invalid, data-disabled, filled/dirty/touched tracking and the form value. This is an improvement rather than a workaround: React Aria shipped two separate implementations that had to be kept in agreement, and the old header documented one place they had already drifted (InputProps redeclared placeholder?: string while TextAreaProps did not).
text-area.tsx.measured: renderToStaticMarkup(<TextArea label="یادداشت" rows={6}/>) → <textarea rows="6" aria-labelledby=…>, gate clean.

search-field.tsx.vendor_available: None. @base-ui/react has no search-field export among its 83 subpaths.

re_authored_behaviours.how: The native HTMLInputElement.prototype value setter, then a bubbling `input` event, then focus.
re_authored_behaviours.why: House rule 5 forbids a useState mirror, and the control must work controlled AND uncontrolled. Assigning el.value = "" directly is swallowed by React's value tracker: no synthetic change fires, the consumer's onChange never runs, and a controlled field snaps back on the next render. The same event is what tells Field.Root the field is no longer filled.
re_authored_behaviours.pinned_by: form-family.test.tsx → 'clears through the platform, so a CONTROLLED consumer is told'. Without the setter that is the only assertion in the file that fails.

re_authored_behaviours.why: RAC bound it; nothing in Base UI does.

re_authored_behaviours.how: Fires onSubmit without preventDefault, so a surrounding <form> keeps its own behaviour.

api_changes.was: Required because RAC composed aria-label="Clear search" from a bundle with no fa entry, unreachable on the server.
api_changes.now: Required because Base UI ships no bundle at all — with no prop the button would be NAMELESS. That is worse than English: there is no Latin word for the HTML gate to catch and a screenshot of a bare × looks like a styling choice.

state_selectors.data-empty (RAC, on the root): → data-filled (Base UI, on Field.Root), POLARITY FLIPPED. `group-data-empty/search:hidden` became `hidden … group-data-filled/search:inline-flex`. Base UI states the positive where RAC stated the negative.

radio-group.tsx.vendor_available: base-vega ships radio-group. Read and not adopted: it is two unlabelled primitives with physical utilities (top-1/2 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2) and no field chrome, no required label, no description. Its two genuinely useful facts — data-checked on Radio.Root and focus-visible on the root — were confirmed against the dist and are what this file now uses.
radio-group.tsx.structure_change: The wrapping <div> that held the flex rules is gone: Base UI's RadioGroup IS the flex container, so listClassName now styles the element carrying role=radiogroup rather than a div beside it. Same public prop, one fewer node.
radio-group.tsx.each_option_names_itself: Radio calls useFieldWiring per option rather than inheriting the group's. Inheriting would point every radio at the GROUP's label and announce five options all called «روش پرداخت». Field.Item's own association is a layout effect, so without this each option is a bare <span role=radio> in the served HTML.

state_selectors.group-data-hovered: → group-hover. The hover target is still the label; only the mechanism changes.
state_selectors.group-data-selected: → data-checked, UN-GROUPED (resubject + rename). Not the same edit toggle.tsx needs: there Base UI spells the persistent ON state data-pressed, which is React Aria's word for the transient pointer-down.
state_selectors.FOCUS_RING (group-data-focus-visible): → FOCUS_RING_SELF. Radio.Root is role=radio and the focusable element; the hidden input is tabindex=-1 aria-hidden. Asserted behaviourally (jsdom does match :focus-visible), tokenised and anchored because `group-data-focus-visible:` CONTAINS the literal `focus-visible:`.
state_selectors.the dot: group/radio named group on Radio.Root. Radio.Indicator is Base UI's answer and mounts CONDITIONALLY, which would replace the scale transition with a mount.

api_changes.kind: CAPABILITY GAP — half the prop's meaning is gone
api_changes.was: One value fed the flex axis AND the arrow-key axis, so a keyboard user could not navigate a direction the layout does not run in.
api_changes.now: Purely visual. Base UI's RadioGroup has no orientation prop: it is a CompositeRoot, useCompositeRoot defaults orientation to 'both' (internals/composite/root/useCompositeRoot.mjs:15), and RadioGroup.mjs does not forward it.
api_changes.severity: widening, not a break — every key that worked still works and the WAI-ARIA radio pattern permits both axes.
api_changes.why_not: @lumo-ui/base-ui-ssr fixes things by passing a public prop. There is no prop to pass.
api_changes.pinned_by: form-family.test.tsx → 'GAP: orientation no longer restricts the arrow-key axis'

api_changes.detail: Base UI's value type is the group's own and can be null; RAC's onChange promised a string. null is normalised to "" rather than widening the public API.

api_changes.reason: Never existed on RAC's RadioFieldProps either; they were destructured in error. The group owns both.

observed_not_fixed.what: At SSR every Radio.Root carries tabindex="-1" — no option is reachable by keyboard before hydration.
observed_not_fixed.evidence: renderToStaticMarkup of a two-option group: both spans tabindex="-1". Base UI's composite assigns the roving 0 after mount. React Aria built its collection during render and emitted 0 on the first option.
observed_not_fixed.why_not: highlightedIndex is a CompositeRoot prop that RadioGroup does not forward.

input-group.tsx.vendor_available: base-vega ships input-group. Read and REJECTED for a third reason on top of the two the file already recorded (compositional so nothing forces a name; physical utilities on every seam): its addon <div> carries an onClick that calls parentElement.querySelector('input').focus() — hand-rolled label-to-control association through the DOM, which is the exact mechanism this migration exists to route around, moved one layer out and made click-only.
input-group.tsx.note: input-group.test.tsx passes UNEDITED, including its aria-describedby, aria-invalid, logical-inset and overlay-count assertions.

link.tsx.why_no_engine: Base UI has no link primitive among its 83 subpaths, so the question was never 'which primitive' but 'does this need one'. Item by item: press handling on a real anchor is re-implementing the browser; data-pressed and data-focus-visible have ZERO files in the Base UI dist and the library's answer everywhere is :active / :focus-visible; the span fallback is three lines; and aria-current is one line, replacing thirty lines of the old header proving React Aria wrote it through despite omitting it from LinkProps. RAC was buying a client-component boundary and nothing else.
link.tsx.won: No "use client". A link in prose, a footer or a server-rendered block now costs the consumer no hydration.

api_changes.verified_unused: grep across packages/blocks, apps/website and packages/ui found no Link call site passing any of them. isDisabled and isCurrent are kept because app-shell.tsx and the nav components pass them.
api_changes.note: onClick and every other native anchor handler still pass through.

state_selectors.data-pressed: → active:. PARTIAL fidelity loss, stated: React Aria's press state survived the pointer leaving and returning; :active ends when the pointer leaves.
state_selectors.data-disabled: KEPT as an attribute — an <a> has no platform disabled state, so the component writes it and may as well keep styling it.
state_selectors.data-current: KEPT and now written by the component. sidebar.test.tsx asserts data-current="true"; navigation-menu.tsx and breadcrumbs.tsx style data-current:.

separator.tsx.vendor_available: base-vega ships separator, and it INHERITS the regression below.
separator.tsx.why_no_engine: The RAC dependency was justified by one thing: the element changes with the orientation, because <hr> is a paragraph-level thematic break and a hand-rolled vertical <hr> announces a break in the reading flow that is not there. @base-ui/react/separator is a REGRESSION on exactly that point — separator/Separator.mjs calls useRenderElement('div', …) unconditionally and adds role=separator, so every separator including the horizontal one becomes a <div>. Plain markup restores <hr> and is one ternary.
separator.tsx.won: No "use client". It ships inside item.tsx and button-group.tsx, both of which are copied into server components.

api_changes.verified_unused: item.tsx and button-group.tsx both extend SeparatorProps and pass only className and orientation; both suites pass unedited.

description-list.tsx.engine: NONE, and it never had one
description-list.tsx.verdict: Engine-independent by construction — four elements and a class list, no "use client", already argued at length in its own header. The Base UI swap has nothing to say about it. data-display.test.tsx's DescriptionList block passes unedited.

gaps_the_adapter_already_closes: Names: every control in this family is aria-labelledby (or, for Select-shaped controls, htmlFor→id) at the FIRST BYTE. Base UI resolves both in layout effects that never run on the server.

Descriptions and errors: aria-describedby lists description then error, in that order, in the served HTML. This is the half with a violation count of zero in every instrument the project owns — an accessible-name rule grades names.

Errors rendering at all: Base UI's Field.Error renders nothing on the server without `match`, because its validity machinery has not run. An authored Persian error message would simply be absent from the first byte.

gaps_base_ui_cannot_do.detail: Field.Root initialises filled as React.useState(false) (field/root/FieldRoot.mjs:45) and FieldRootProps exposes controlled overrides for dirty and touched and NONE for filled. A server-rendered SearchField with a defaultValue serves its clear button hidden. Alternatives rejected: a useState mirror (rule 5, and it fights the uncontrolled case) and :placeholder-shown (a real CSS answer that silently does nothing when the caller passes no placeholder — a control that works only when an unrelated optional prop is set is worse than a documented gap).
gaps_base_ui_cannot_do.pinned_by: form-family.test.tsx → 'GAP: data-filled is absent from the first byte'

gaps_base_ui_cannot_do.detail: Base UI's Separator is always a <div>. Closed by dropping the engine, not by the adapter.
No press abstraction exists in Base UI at all (button/ButtonDataAttributes declares `disabled` and nothing else). :active is the platform's and ends when the pointer leaves.

verification.tsc: clean for all nine owned files across packages/ui, packages/blocks and apps/website. Remaining monorepo errors are in disclosure.tsx, index.ts's hover-card re-export and demos.tsx's Autocomplete — all other agents' files, all pre-existing.

failures_not_mine.menubar.test.tsx: 3 failures. menubar.tsx is another agent's Base UI migration; its triggers are now role=menuitem and the toolbar role is gone.
failures_not_mine.autocomplete.test.tsx: 2 POISON TWIN failures asserting bare Base UI's Intl filter does not fold Persian. autocomplete.tsx was edited at 09:55 by another agent.
failures_not_mine.data-display.test.tsx + controls.test.ts: Appeared only after table.tsx (09:58) and toast.tsx (09:55) were edited mid-run by other agents. Cause is `TypeError: First argument to Intl.Locale constructor can't be empty` thrown from core's direction() via table.tsx. These suites PASSED against this branch's form.tsx at 09:53.

verification.registry: scripts/build-registry.mjs re-run — link and separator correctly lose their react-aria-components dependency. The diff also picks up other agents' in-flight migrations, because registry.json is generated from the whole tree.
